new.n: Civil War baker's buried fortune, old house razed for the Knights of Columbus hall, Racine
new.pl: Probably 320 Fifth St, Racine: the Knights of Columbus hall listed there by 1931, on the site the council bought in Nov 1922 (inferred from city directories; the 1922 story gives no street)
new.v: A pre-Civil War baker's cashed-in savings (amount not given)
new.st: In 1922, as the Knights of Columbus prepared to raze an old house 'on one of the principal streets' for their new clubhouse, the owning family told the story: a miserly German baker built it before the Civil War, cashed his securities after Bull Run, buried the money somewhere inside the house, and died before the war ended without telling where. His widow dug in the basement for months until her death; later owners forbade digging for fear of the walls. The Knights said the gold would turn up when the foundation was dug. No find was reported.
new.t: Urban lot, built over by the 1920s hall: look only. The address is inferred, not printed.
